pure-announcement.rationale: This is the original 1973 MITRE/Air Force technical report establishing a formal mathematical model of computer security, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest existing concepts (agent security as OS security, datasheets for datasets, current-state grounding, shared mental-model erosion, agent tool ergonomics, answer-layer interception) cover multi-level confidentiality access control or a no-write-down/no-read-up rule; this is a distinct idea.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The model is a rigorous mathematical formalization with explicit definitions and proofs that a reader can check directly, not an unsourced claim.

durability.rationale: The confidentiality access-control model this report founded in 1973 (formalizing 'security' and 'compromise') has remained the standard reference for multi-level security for over five decades and is still directly implemented in production systems today, including the very product (Omnigent) whose docs cited it implicitly.

actionability.rationale: It specifies a concrete, implementable access rule set (a subject may not write information to an object at a lower classification than material it has read) that a builder can apply directly when designing any confinement or data-leak-prevention mechanism.

atomicity.rationale: The extractable core idea — once a session has read protected material, its subsequent writes are confined to that same protection scope — is statable in one paragraph independent of this report's general-systems-theory framing.
